hook: NASA ripped this capsule off a rocket faster than sound.
narration: This capsule was torn off its rocket at faster than the speed of sound.
It was NASA's Ascent Abort 2 test, and the capsule was a test version with nobody inside.
The booster lifted it off the pad and pushed it past Mach one.
The tower on top is a launch abort system, rocket motors built to pull a crew away from a failing rocket.
At thirty one thousand feet, the abort fired and yanked the capsule clear of the booster.
[short pause] Then the tower let go, and the capsule fell. On this test, it had no parachutes.
outcome: NASA said the test showed the abort system can pull a capsule to safety during launch.
title: Capsule torn off a rocket at Mach 1
description:
On July 2, 2019, NASA's Ascent Abort-2 flight test fired Orion's launch abort system during a climb past the speed of sound, pulling a test capsule away from its booster. No one was aboard.

Footage: NASA KSC video, via NASA Image and Video Library: https://images.nasa.gov/details/KSC-20190702-MH-NAS01-0001-Ascent_Abort-2_Test_Launch_ISO_B-Roll-3218294

question_comment: Would you trust an abort system to pull you off a failing rocket?

extra_sources.excerpt: During the flight, a test version of the Orion crew module will be launched atop a booster. At 31,000 feet in altitude, the launch abort system will activate to pull the capsule away from the booster and orient it for splashdown.

About 27 seconds after the abort is initiated and the Orion elements separate from the booster, the launch abort system’s jettison motor is seen firing, releasing the capsule. The July 2 test demonstrated the Orion’s launch abort system works during high-stress aerodynamic conditions and can pull the capsule to safety if an emergency ever arises during launch.
